Definition: from G4561; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft:--fleshly.
BiblicalUsage: Sarkinos is fleshly too, but it names what is made of flesh rather than what is ruled by it. Paul could not speak to the Corinthians as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal, even as unto babes in Christ; and he says believers are the epistle of Christ, written not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart. Hebrews sets the contrast: a priest made not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the difference between the two fleshly words is the difference between a babe and a man. The law written on stone was carnal and could not give life; the Spirit writes on the heart, and that is what makes a priest forever. What strikes me is that God does not settle for stone tablets — He writes on flesh, on hearts that live.
